# Set up Crosshead for Codex

<!-- Generated by scripts/host-plugins.mjs; do not edit. -->

This plugin contains only hooks and this skill. The hooks run the Crosshead
runtime installed on this machine (`~/.crosshead` unless `CROSSHEAD_HOME` is
set). One runtime, daemon and identity is shared by Claude Code, Codex, Hermes,
OpenCode and Pi. Setup installs that runtime and connects it to Codex.

Run each command with your shell tool. Use `"${CROSSHEAD_HOME:-$HOME/.crosshead}/bin/crosshead"`
for `crosshead` if it is not on PATH.

1. Check the current state: `crosshead doctor`. If the runtime is installed and
   the `codex_hooks` check is ok with `mode=plugin`, setup is already
   done; report that and stop.
2. Explain the next two steps to the user and ask for explicit consent. Do not
   continue without a clear yes.
   - The installer is downloaded from https://crosshead.sh/install and run with
     bash. It downloads one release tarball, checks its SHA-256 against the
     digest pinned in the installer, installs three npm dependencies with install
     scripts disabled, and writes wrappers to `~/.crosshead/bin`. Runtimes
     never update themselves.
   - Quickstart creates a local identity if there is none (its private key stays
     in `~/.crosshead`), registers it with the hosted service at
     https://crosshead.sh and starts the local daemon. An existing identity is
     reused.
3. Install or update the runtime:

   ```sh
   curl -fsSL https://crosshead.sh/install | bash
   ```

4. Connect Codex:

   ```sh
   crosshead quickstart --api-base https://crosshead.sh --adapter codex --workspace-root . --hook-mode plugin
   ```

   `--hook-mode plugin` keeps quickstart from writing its own Codex hooks
   (this plugin provides them). When the plugin is enabled for the user (the
   default for a plugin install) it also removes Crosshead hooks an earlier
   install wrote. Either way each event is captured once.
5. Verify with `crosshead doctor`. Expect `codex_hooks` to report `mode=plugin`.
   Until Codex has run the plugin hooks, that check warns that no plugin hook
   invocation has been seen; the next step resolves it.
   Report any other failed check to the user verbatim; do not work around it.
6. Codex runs plugin hooks only after you trust them. Ask the user to open `/hooks`, review the Crosshead hooks and trust them. A changed plugin version needs a new review. Until Codex has run them, quickstart keeps any Crosshead hooks an earlier install wrote; rerun `crosshead install codex` after the first session to remove those.
7. Start a new Codex session so the hooks load with the runtime in place.

Other hosts and scripts keep using `curl -fsSL https://crosshead.sh/install | bash`
followed by `crosshead quickstart --adapter <host>`. Remove Crosshead from
Codex by uninstalling this plugin; `crosshead uninstall` removes the runtime.
